title: GPU Pool Guardian: Mini Ops Playbook and Compact Controls for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Design a compact, mobile-friendly 'Guardian' mini-playbook within Redwood Console for Dedicated GPU pools. The feature bundles key health signals, one-click autoscale actions, burst tuning presets, and a lightweight runbook card so SREs and platform engineers can triage and act from a single surface. Scope: 1) mini-dashboard header with SLO strip, queue depth, and thermal indicator; 2) compact burst/policy editor with 3 curated presets and a custom slider; 3) safe action flow (canary scale, drain + fallback) with inline warnings and link-to-rollout; 4) embedded quick-run diagnostics that trigger predefined telemetry captures; 5) accessibility and keyboard-first interactions. The design must work inside existing pool details page and as a collapsed micro-panel for quick ops. Deliverables: Figma prototype (desktop + narrow), clickable flows for canary scale + fallback, component spec, acceptance criteria, and handoff tokens for frontend engineering. Prioritization notes: keep first iteration focused on read+act flows; defer advanced forecasting charts to follow-up.
acceptance_criteria: Guardian mini-panel renders in pool details and when collapsed from pool list
SLO strip shows 30/60/90s latency and error rate; values match telemetry within 5%
Three burst presets available (Conservative, Balanced, Aggressive) and a custom slider; changes create a draft policy and a link to rollout
Safe action flow enforces a canary node target and shows estimated capacity impact before confirmation
Diagnostics button triggers telemetry snapshot (trace id returned and visible in UI) and links to the relevant dashboard
Keyboard users can open the panel, switch presets, and confirm actions without a mouse
Design tokens and spacing match console design system; components handed off with CSS vars and example states
